summary: A 20-foot pole platform on Thomas Hill, a patrol point for Linfor Hill, built in 1934 and abandoned in 1950; it has since fallen over, leaving footings and railings.

facts.status_note: Platform has fallen over; cement footings, pole legs and railings remain

visit.trail_note: Listed as hike-in; no source describes whether the public may visit today

evidence.supports: Served as a patrol point for the Linfor Hill Lookout
evidence.quote: Thomas Hill Lookout served as a Patrol Point for the Linfor Hill Lookout.

evidence.supports: Platform built 1934 and abandoned 1950; 20-foot pole platform
evidence.quote: The 20′ pole platform was built in 1934 and abandoned in 1950.

evidence.supports: Platform has fallen over but still exists
evidence.quote: Surprising this platform still exists, although it has fallen over.

evidence.supports: Cement footings, pole legs and railings remain
evidence.quote: The cement footings, pole legs, and railings are all still here and recognizable.

evidence.supports: Elevation 4450 feet, in Coeur d'Alene National Forest
Patrol point about a mile southeast of the Linfor Hill tower
evidence.quote: 1 mile Southeast of the tower is a patrol point on Thomas Hill.

evidence.supports: Linfor Hill tower built in 1934 (30-foot pole L-4)

notes_for_editor: Every Thomas Hill fact comes from one Idaho Fire Lookouts page (a 2022 post); the Linfor Hill page is cited only for the patrol-point relation and the Linfor tower's 1934 build. The agency is taken from the forest named on the elevation line, which the page does not label as an agency. The record has no county or agency; no correction is proposed. Status is recorded as ruins because the platform has fallen and only footings, pole legs and railings remain. The page's photo is captioned as Ned Hill Lookout, so it is not used. No staffing history is given for this site.
